source_review.notes: Checked all thirteen primary references. Current OpenTelemetry specifications support independent signals with shared context, Resource identity for the observed entity, semantic-convention/schema evolution, sampling decision/recording distinctions, and structured log fields including source/observed time and trace correlation. Current Collector exporter-helper documentation supports bounded queues, batching, timeouts, retries, enqueue-failure/drop behavior, and optional persistent queues without an exactly-once guarantee. Current Prometheus/OpenMetrics documentation supports one quantity/unit per metric family, unique label-set series, bounded-cardinality guidance, aggregatable histograms, counter reset semantics, and exemplars. W3C Trace Context supports traceparent/tracestate interoperability plus explicit privacy/trust-boundary concerns. Kubernetes provides a current governed metrics reference.

invariant_checking.notes: All declared question, identity, metric, event, context, sampling, pipeline, application-impact, governance, and alert invariants remain consistent.

proof_review.notes: The chapter states no theorem and contains no deductive proof; its assurance chain remains conditional on instrumentation, clocks, propagation, sampling, collectors, schemas, storage, queries, and human assumptions.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No proof sketch is claimed; cardinality and buffer formulas are explicitly upper-bound/sizing models with stated exclusions rather than correctness or durability proofs.

evidence: The executable observability inventory is labeled synthetic and explicitly disclaims control effectiveness.
The cardinality, percentile, identity, redaction, sampling, queue, tenancy, stale-alert, change, and schema-removal examples are scenarios rather than production observations.
Standards and implementation semantics, platform recommendations, symbolic models, synthetic controls, and required operational measurements remain distinguishable.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production telemetry, secret/personal record, trace, metric series, collector queue, backend query, alert, incident, cost, or deletion result is claimed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter consistently treats observability as inference from fallible evidence, distinguishes observed resource from emitter, event from observed time, instrument from aggregation, correlation from identity/causation, sampled intent from storage, and retention from erasure.

practitioner_review.notes: A practitioner can contract questions/signals, standardize identity/semantics, instrument bounded metrics/events/traces, govern cardinality/context/sampling, build resilient tenant pipelines, protect data/time semantics, correlate change, define SLO alerts/views, govern retention/cost, self-observe, test, migrate, and retire.

pedagogical_review.notes: The sequence progresses from questions/contracts through identity/conventions, metrics/cardinality, events/traces/context/sampling, instrumentation and pipelines, buffering/tenancy/privacy/time, change/SLO/views/retention, self-observation/testing, and operations. Ten examples cover unbounded labels, percentile aggregation, resource identity, redaction timing, sampling bias, queue overload, tenant trust, freshness, change identity, and schema consumers. Five exercises progress from definitions through evidence tracing, diagnosis, architecture trade-offs, and backend/schema migration, with complete model answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
